quote: neither of us reveal what went on inside
content:
An unverifiable demonstration cannot bear a general safety conclusion
The accounts can challenge a literal claim that these particular volunteers could never be persuaded, if the reported outcomes are accepted. The chapter does not provide transcripts, a reproducible method or an independent audit. It therefore cannot estimate a general escape rate or show that every containment design with different communication rules must fail.

Resolve does not change the probability laws
The refusal to pretend that determination guarantees success is essential. Read the exhortation together with the author’s admissions of failure and emotional cost. Once those are preserved, the defensible message is permission to investigate difficult problems; the text does not demonstrate a transferable ability to solve them.

quote: believe that you will solve the problem with probability 1
content:
Low confidence and serious effort can coexist coherently
A person can assign a small probability to success and still work hard when the upside or information gained warrants it. No temporary belief in one’s own impossibility proof is necessary. The rational question is the expected value of this attempt compared with alternatives, including what failure will teach.

Keep all five reported trials in the denominator
The author reports two earlier wins, then one win and two losses in three further games with offers of thousands of dollars. The account is therefore three wins in five described attempts, not invincibility and not exclusively trivial stakes. A tiny, selected, heterogeneous series remains unsuitable for a stable probability estimate; the disclosed failures deserve to stay visible.
